title: Index Pairs of a String
statement:
Find every place where one of the strings in `words` appears inside `text`. Each appearance is reported as a pair `[i, j]` of indices such that the slice of `text` from position `i` through position `j` (both included) equals some word. Overlapping appearances all count, and one start index may begin several different words.

Return the list of all such pairs sorted by `i`, and by `j` when two pairs share the same `i`. Return an empty list when no word appears.
constraints: text and every words[i] contain only lowercase English letters
All strings in words are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

The direct method searches `text` once for every word, then sorts all the matches. A trie (prefix tree) turns this around: store all the words in one tree, then from each start index `i` walk forward through `text` and through the tree together. Every node that ends a word gives a pair, and the walk stops as soon as no word continues with the next letter. Because `i` grows in the outer loop and `j` in the inner one, the pairs come out already sorted.

## Approach

1. Build the trie: each node has a `next` map from letter to child and an `isWord` flag.
2. Insert every word, creating missing children, and set `isWord` on the node of its last letter.
3. For each start `i`, set `node` to the root and move `j` from `i` to the end of `text`.
4. Step to the child for `text[j]`; if it does not exist, no word starts with `text[i..j]`, so stop this start.
5. If the node ends a word, add `[i, j]` to `pairs`.
6. Return `pairs`.

## Example 1, step by step

The trie holds `story`, `fleet` and `leetcode`. Starts `0` to `2` (`t`, `h`, `e`) have no child under the root. At `i = 3` the letters `s, t, o, r, y` follow the tree to the end of `story`, giving `[3, 7]`. At `i = 9` the walk spells `fleet` (`[9, 13]`), and at `i = 10` it spells `leetcode` (`[10, 17]`). The result is `[[3,7],[9,13],[10,17]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(W + n · L): building costs the total word length W, and each of the n starts walks at most L letters, the longest word length.
- Space: O(W) for the trie, plus the output.

## Pitfalls

- Matches can overlap and share a start (`"ab"` and `"aba"` both at 0); do not stop at the first word found.
- Keep walking after a match: a longer word may continue past it.
- If you collect matches word by word, sort them by start and then by end before returning.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` | the empty-prefix node of the trie |
| `node` | the current trie node |
| `ch` | a letter of the word being inserted |
| `i`, `j` | start and current end index in `text` |
| `pairs` | the index pairs found, in sorted order |
